title: Load-gen person properties must have a single writer per key (parity runs)
answers: Shadow parity run reports property divergence on dangerous-merge pairs
Why does the load generator write loadgen_last_update_<user>?
Can I add a shared person property to capture-load-gen events?
body:
Invariant: every person property key the load generator writes must have exactly one writer (one user / one partition).
Enforced in rust/capture-load-gen/src/event.rs:EventFactory::person_update_event, which writes `loadgen_last_update_{user}` using the distinct_id.
Why: merged (dangerous-merge) pairs are written from two partitions, and each backend applies the writes in its own arrival order. A shared key therefore ends with different last values per backend, and verify reports a false property divergence.
Per-seed keys already follow the same shape. Any new property the generator sets should be keyed per user or per seed, not shared.
applies: rust/capture-load-gen event generation, especially $set payloads compared in shadow parity runs
says: Person property divergence appears after merging in load testing runs
New load generator properties show different values between backend instances
Which properties can a load test write to safely together

search: Load generator person property consistency invariant: rust/capture-load-gen/src/event.rs:EventFactory enforces exactly one writer per property key (one user or one partition) via loadgen_last_update_{user} keying. Merged (dangerous-merge) pairs written from two partitions cause each backend to apply writes in its own arrival order, resulting in different final values and false property divergence in parity verify reports. Per-seed and per-user keys already follow the required shape; any new property set via $set payloads must be keyed per user or per seed, never shared across partitions. This constraint is critical for shadow parity run validation.
